question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in sandbox-to-ACP bridge now, fold sandboxed ACP into the broader execution-backend/runtime design, or keep ACP blocked from sandboxed sessions?
rationale: The request crosses from container-isolated agent execution into host-side process execution and would define public security, config, and tool contracts that automation should not choose.

options.title: Design Narrow Bridge
options.body: Define an explicit opt-in host bridge with requester allowlisting, spawn/steer/cancel verbs, audit logs, rate limits, docs, and live Docker/acpx proof.

options.title: Fold Into Execution Backends
options.body: Use the broader backend/profile or ACP-runtime work as the design home and keep this issue as the sandboxed ACP acceptance case.

options.title: Keep Blocked
options.body: Preserve the current fail-closed behavior and document that ACP must run from non-sandboxed sessions or inside a separately sandboxed harness setup.

recommendation.title: Design Narrow Bridge
recommendation.body: Define an explicit opt-in host bridge with requester allowlisting, spawn/steer/cancel verbs, audit logs, rate limits, docs, and live Docker/acpx proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined history across sessions_spawn, ACP sandbox docs, slash-command policy, and the security/product boundary language.
